claim: In the AWS Security Reference Architecture, the Security Tooling account is the delegated administrator (through AWS Organizations) for security services managed in an administrator/member structure, including AWS Config, GuardDuty, Macie, Security Hub, Security Hub CSPM, Detective and Inspector.
question: In the AWS Security Reference Architecture, which account runs GuardDuty, Security Hub, Macie, Inspector, Detective and Config as delegated administrator?

values.display: The Security Tooling account serves as the administrator account
AWS Organizations delegated administrator functionality

evidence.quote: The Security Tooling account serves as the administrator account for security services that are managed in an administrator/member structure throughout the AWS accounts. As mentioned earlier, this is handled through the AWS Organizations delegated administrator functionality.

Services in the AWS SRA that currently support delegated administrator include IAM centralized management of root access, AWS Config, AWS Firewall Manager, Amazon GuardDuty, IAM Access Analyzer, Amazon Macie, AWS Security Hub, AWS Security Hub CSPM, Amazon Detective, AWS Audit Manager, Amazon Inspector, AWS CloudTrail, and AWS Systems Manager.

claim: Security Hub CSPM recommends aligning the delegated administrator accounts of services such as Detective with its own; if the administrator accounts of Detective and Security Hub CSPM are not aligned, navigating from findings into Detective does not work.
question: Why should Detective and Security Hub CSPM use the same delegated administrator account?

values.display: recommends aligning the delegated administrator accounts
navigating from findings into Detective will not work

evidence.quote: Security Hub CSPM recommends aligning the delegated administrator accounts for services such as Detective (where they exist) for smoother integration. For example, if you do not align administrator accounts between Detective and Security Hub CSPM, navigating from findings into Detective will not work.

claim: In the AWS Security Reference Architecture, GuardDuty is enabled in all accounts through AWS Organizations, findings are managed in the delegated administrator (Security Tooling) account, and active findings are exported to a central S3 bucket in the Log Archive account, encrypted with a KMS customer managed key, so they are retained beyond 90 days.
question: How does the AWS Security Reference Architecture keep GuardDuty findings for longer than GuardDuty does?

values.display: GuardDuty is enabled in all accounts through AWS Organizations
exported to a central S3 bucket in the Log Archive account
retain the findings beyond 90 days
values.spoken: keep the findings beyond ninety days

evidence.quote: In the AWS SRA, GuardDuty is enabled in all accounts through AWS Organizations, and all findings are viewable and actionable by appropriate security teams in the GuardDuty delegated administrator account (in this case, the Security Tooling account). GuardDuty active findings are exported to a central S3 bucket in the Log Archive account, so you can retain the findings beyond 90 days.

note: d012, d105. KMS customer managed key encryption is stated in the next sentence of the same paragraph.

claim: In the AWS Security Reference Architecture, the AWS Config delegated administrator is the Security Tooling account, and the Config delivery channel delivers configuration snapshots to a central S3 bucket in the Log Archive account.
question: Where does the AWS Security Reference Architecture send AWS Config configuration snapshots?

values.display: the AWS Config delegated administrator account is the Security Tooling account
a centralized S3 bucket in the Log Archive account

evidence.quote: In the AWS SRA, the AWS Config delegated administrator account is the Security Tooling account. The AWS Config delivery channel is configured to deliver resource configuration snapshots in a centralized S3 bucket in the Log Archive account.

claim: With Macie managed through AWS Organizations, the delegated administrator can enable or suspend Macie in any account, create discovery jobs for member buckets and view all policy findings, but sensitive data findings can be viewed only by the account that created the sensitive data discovery job.
question: In a Macie organization, who can see sensitive data findings?

values.display: view all policy findings for all member accounts
Sensitive data findings can be viewed only by the account that created the sensitive findings job.

evidence.quote: Principals who have the appropriate permissions in the delegated administrator account (in this case, the Security Tooling account) can enable or suspend Macie in any account, create sensitive data discovery jobs for buckets that are owned by member accounts, and view all policy findings for all member accounts. Sensitive data findings can be viewed only by the account that created the sensitive findings job.

claim: Macie is optimized for scanning objects in Amazon S3; data from other sources, such as RDS or Aurora snapshot exports or exported DynamoDB tables, can be moved to S3 and then evaluated by Macie.
question: How can Macie find sensitive data that lives in RDS or DynamoDB?

values.display: Macie is optimized for scanning objects in Amazon S3.
can be moved to Amazon S3 and evaluated by Macie

evidence.quote: Macie is optimized for scanning objects in Amazon S3. As a result, any Macie-supported object type that can be placed in Amazon S3 (permanently or temporarily) can be scanned for sensitive data. This means that data from other sources—for example, periodic snapshot exports of Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) or Amazon Aurora databases, exported Amazon DynamoDB tables, or extracted text files from native or third-party applications—can be moved to Amazon S3 and evaluated by Macie.

claim: If S3 objects are encrypted with a KMS key that you manage, you add the Macie service-linked role as a key user of that key so Macie can scan the data.
question: What must you do so Macie can scan S3 objects encrypted with your customer managed KMS key?

values.display: add the Macie service-linked role as a key user

qualifiers.condition: objects encrypted with a customer managed KMS key

evidence.quote: If S3 objects are encrypted with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that you manage, you can add the Macie service-linked role as a key user to that KMS key to enable Macie to scan the data.

claim: The Detective administrator account can automatically enable all current organization accounts as Detective members and add new accounts as they join the organization; it can also invite accounts outside the organization in the same Region.
question: Does Amazon Detective automatically cover new accounts that join the organization?

values.display: automatically enable all current member accounts
add new member accounts as they get added to the AWS organization

evidence.quote: The Detective administrator account has the ability to automatically enable all current member accounts in the organization as Detective member accounts, and also add new member accounts as they get added to the AWS organization. Detective administrator accounts also have the ability to invite member accounts that currently do not reside in the AWS organization, but are within the same Region, to contribute their data to the primary account's behavior graph.

claim: AWS Artifact does not support the delegated administration feature; instead you restrict it to IAM roles of the audit and compliance teams, and IAM policies can limit specific roles to specific reports.
question: Can AWS Artifact be managed by an Organizations delegated administrator account?

values.display: AWS Artifact doesn't support the delegated administration feature.
access to only specific AWS Artifact reports through IAM policies

evidence.quote: AWS Artifact doesn't support the delegated administration feature. Instead, you can restrict this capability to only IAM roles in the Security Tooling account that pertain to your audit and compliance teams, so they can download, review, and provide those reports to external auditors as needed. You can additionally restrict specific IAM roles to have access to only specific AWS Artifact reports through IAM policies.

claim: In the Well-Architected security pillar, detection has two parts: unexpected or unwanted configuration changes, and unexpected behavior; for unexpected behavior, GuardDuty alerts you when unexpected and potentially unauthorized or malicious activity occurs in your AWS accounts.
question: Where does GuardDuty fit in the Well-Architected security pillar's detection guidance?

values.display: Detection consists of two parts
Using Amazon GuardDuty, you can be alerted

evidence.quote: Detection consists of two parts: detection of unexpected or unwanted configuration changes, and the detection of unexpected behavior.
Using Amazon GuardDuty, you can be alerted when unexpected and potentially unauthorized or malicious activity occurs within your AWS accounts.

note: d013. The pillar's best practices are SEC04-BP01 to BP04 (logging, standardized locations, correlate and enrich alerts, remediate non-compliant resources).
